newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity moves higher on physical power.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity moves higher on physical power.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures continued a recent climb to new highs Wednesdays as front-month contracts took strength from robust physical power prices in the U.S. West, industry sources said.

"At this point in time there doesn't seem to be much reason for this market to come off," said one New York-based futures trader, noting that power demand was strong in the Southwest and that some Western power generation was down for maintenance.
As of 1220 EDT, June Palo Verde (PV) futures were trading up 40 cents at $22.90 after hitting a new contract high of $23.00 and trade at a low of $22.45 per megawatt hour (MWh).
Sources said the June PV contract was likely to find some strong resistance at the new high of $23.00 per MWh.
July PV was trading up 40 cents at $26.15 after hitting a new contract high of $26.25 and reaching as low as $25.95 per MWh.

June California Oregon Border (COB) was up 27 cents at $16.60 per MWh after hitting a new contract high of $16.65 and reaching as low as $16.30, while July was up 26 cents at the day's high of $18.15 after reaching as low as $18.05 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1135 EDT an estimated total of 171 COB and 239 PV contracts had traded.
As of 1215 EDT, NYMEX June Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading up 4.1 cents at $2.35 per million British thermal units.

The strength in futures in recent days continued to be attributed to strong Western physical power prices, particularily in the Southwest where maximum temperatures of over 100 degrees Fahrenheit in Arizona the past few days have boosted air conditioning demand.

Generation capacity in the western U.S. also was limited, with an estimated total of about 8,000 megawatts (MW) of power output said to be offline for repairs or maintenance. However, much of the idled capacity was expected to return to service later this month.
Also, a 750 MW unit at the coal-fired Four Corners power plant in Arizona was nearing restart Wednesday morning after tripping off line late Tuesday, Arizona Public Service said.
The unit was expected to return to full power by about 1200 PDT (1300 EDT), the company said.
In the Pacific Northwest, dry weather was forecast through Sunday with temperatures expected to be three to six degrees above normal.
In the Southwest, above and much-above normal temperatures were expected with no precipitation through Sunday.
COB open interest for May 6 rose 200 to 5,035, while PV open interest rose 15 to 5,674, NYMEX said.
